Farmington River Regional School District
School Committee
Special Planning and Strategy Work Session
Meeting #482 Farmington River Elementary School Library
Monday, July 20, 2026
MINUTES 6:30 PM
Members Present: Carl Nett, Denise Hardie, Douglas Miner, Stacey Schultze, Kate Meierdiercks
Also Present: Timothy Lee, Superintendent
1. Call to Order:
D. Hardie called the meeting to order at 6:30
2. Public Comment
D. Hardie stated the importance of including the public and members of the school staff and
community in the important conversations related to leadership transitions and configurations.
D. Miner agreed.
3. Review/Approval of Minutes
Regular meeting of 6/7/2026.
MOTION to APPROVE: C. Nett
D. Hardie asked for the Committee to clarify the meeting time of regular meetings: 6:30 or 6:00.
Discussion and agreement that 6:00 shall be the meeting time of regular meetings for
2026-2027.
SECOND as revised: S. Schultze
APPROVED: Unanimous
Meeting Date for August: Mr. Lee asked the Committee to change the meeting date for August
to the second Monday (8/10) instead of the first.
MOTION: C. Nett moves that the August meeting date be the 10th of August instead of the 3rd.
SECOND: S. Schultze
APPROVED: Unanimous
4. Superintendent’s Report
(H) indicates “handout,” supporting document
* If technical or network issues preclude the use of Zoom, the meeting may continue in person only.
Pg. 1 of 3
a. Staffing Changes: Mr. Lee summarized some staffing shifts for the new school year: Ms.
Hamill reassigned to first grade to fill the resignation of Ms. Martin. Ms. Loubier to PreK
EK to fill the vacancy left by Ms. Hammil’s reassignment. Mr Scaglione hired as
paraprofessional to fill resignation of Ms. Krans. Ms. Goulange hired as assistant to the
superintendent/principal after Ms. Stamm reassigned to .8FTE Art/Music. One position
possibly pending to position of EC Co-teacher. Mr. Miner suggested that since a school
committee member’s relative was hired into the role, a review of state ethics guidelines
be conducted to see if some sort of disclosure is indicated.
b. Financial FY26 indicators: the year ended well in the black with tuitions, personnel and
curriculum from School Choice revolving in good shape.
c. State budget process ended well with supplemental FY26 Rural Aid allocated to FRRSD
for FY26 and FY27 use.
d. FY27 Rural Aid per Governor’s budget based on allocation of $20M state-wide. Could
mean more for us in FY27.
e. Circuit Breaker also up per final adopted state budget in Conference Committee.
f. Capital updates: PA System repair complete. New van expected in next week.
S. Schultze brought up the topic of window film for intruder protection. Asked to keep this topic on the
agenda for future meetings.
5. New Business:
a. Action on Treasurer Appointment: Mr. Lee recommended the appointment of Sharon
Harrison to the position of Treasurer to replace Jane Gleason who is retiring after more
than 30 years of service to the district.
MOTION to approve Superintendent’s recommendation: C. Nett
SECOND: D. Miner
APPROVED: Unanimous
Mr. Lee shared that the Committee should expect a hire annual cost that is significantly
higher than the current treasurer compensation at about $10,800 per year.
6. Old Business
Mr. Lee led a strategy session re current issues and responding to district leadership transition.
a. Current conditions.
Mr. Lee shared worksheet to review current conditions and solicit input from members.
Assets/positives: fiscal stability, improving student outcomes, operational/transportation
improving, engaged PTA and community, ability to be flexible/use creative solutions.
Challenges: declining enrollment, staffing our rural, far-removed school, unable to
implement some curriculum topics (e.g. world language.) pending capital liabilities.
Aftercare and staffing challenges.
(H) indicates “handout,” supporting document
* If technical or network issues preclude the use of Zoom, the meeting may continue in person only.
Pg. 2 of 3
b. Mr. Lee shared a document intended to serve as a guide to the different options
available for filling the superintendent role into the 2027-2028 school year. Options on
this document included options to replace the part-time role in the same way, with
another part-time superintendent, combining the role of DSS and Supt, combining the
role of Principal/Supt, entering a shared superintendent relationship with another district
or joining an existing superintendency union, or possible reconfiguration to join another
regional district.
There was significant discussion and questions on these options.
The Committee did not make a choice as to which model to pursue but consensus
showed that the options of shared superintendency and/or joining a superintendency
union or other regions; were not favored at this time. The Committee asked Mr. Lee to
seek more information about the options of Principal/Superintendent and
DSS/Superintendent from districts that use this model (Richmond and Hancock,
respectively).
c. An agenda item re: ‘Grant Options for Consolidation/Regionalization Studies’ was not
discussed.
7. Adjournment
MOTION to ADJOURN at 8:28 pm: C. Nett
SECOND: S. Shultze
APPROVED: Unanimous
(H) indicates “handout,” supporting document
* If technical or network issues preclude the use of Zoom, the meeting may continue in person only.

MINUTES
Otis Cultural Council
July 15, 2026
This meeting was conducted in person.
I. Call to Order: 6:08 p.m. Present: Carole Burke, Shanon Albee, Deb Fogel, Susan
Hicks, Margie Klein
II. Approval of the minutes of May 20, 2026 Deb Fogel approved the minutes, and
Susan Hicks seconded the motion. The minutes were approved.
III. Chair Report (Carole):
A. Jeanne and Shanon have closed out FY26 reimbursements. All town funds have
been spent. We received $6,000 from the town on July 1.
B. New Grant Season begins on September 1. The information has been sent to the
Otis Observer.
IV. Financial Report (Shanon):
A. Shanon is waiting to close out the books. We have spent all of the town money.
V. Feedback about Otis Celebration Day/June 13 (Susan, Margie, Carole)
A. Susan, Margie, and Carole reported that it was an amazing event. The Grouse
House did a great job, and the vendors were terrific.
B. The music and the sound system were amazing.
C. All agreed that the event was too long.
D. The Garden Center donated plants. Everyone agreed that there will need to be a
schedule and more volunteers for the planting activity.
VI. Beautify Otis Program
A. All of the barrels have been planted. Carole will send an email thanking the
gardeners for volunteering.
VII. Other Business
A. Recycling needs more volunteers.
B. There was a discussion about a holiday party.
C. The Amvets have requested a grant for the music for the anniversary celebration.
These funds would have to come from recycling. The committee voted to
support the music, but not the DJ.
D. They will have to fill out a reimbursement form and a short narrative
documenting the reason for the grant.
VIII. The meeting was adjourned at 7:08 p.m.
Minutes submitted by Carole Burke

--- MINUTES ---

Farmington River Regional School District
School Committee
Meeting #483 Farmington River Elementary School Library
Monday, August 10th, 2026
MINUTES
6:00 PM
Members Present: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett
Also Present: Superintendent Timothy Lee, Caroline Stamm
Absent: Douglas Miner, Stacey Schultze
1. Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 6:00 PM by Superintendent Lee.
a. Roll Call: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett.
i. Douglas Miner and Stacey Schultze were not present.
2. Public Comment:
a. There was no public comment at this time.
3. Review of Minutes:
- Special Planning and Work Session Meeting (7/20/26)
a. The review of the minutes from the Special Planning & Work Session Meeting held on
7/20/26 has been postponed to the next meeting.
4. Superintendent’s Report:
a. 2026-2027 Staffing Update: Superintendent Lee provided a recap of the staffing changes.
i. The resignation of the 1st grade teacher position has been filled by Rebecca
Hamill (former PK/EK teacher).
ii. The PK/EK Teacher position was filled by Madison Loubier (former Student
Teacher/Para).
iii. The Admin Team decided to hire an Early Childhood Co-Teacher to help support
the load in PK/EK. They filled the position with Maggie Avery, a new teacher to
the industry, Otis-native, and FRRSD graduate.
b. Projected 2026-2027 Opening Enrollment
i. Superintendent Lee provided an overview of the K-6 opening enrollment
projections, noting students thjat we know who have left the district, and new
incoming students. He also noted that our PK/EK numbers are up, which is
promising and that overall, our numbers are about even compared to last year.
c. Transportation Update
i. Mike Saporito, Caroline Stamm, and Terrie Gardino from Dufour have been in
conversation regarding transportation, and we are on track to post routes by the
end of the week.
d. LYA Afterschool Staffing Activity/Update
i. Sharon from the LYA has had some good interviews for staffing the after-school
program, and we still have an advertisement out with the Shoppers Guide and
are optimistic to get more. The licensure paperwork is continuing on track as well.
FRRSD School Committee Meeting #483 - 8.10.2026 1 of 3
ii. The committee discussed other ways to get the word out about staffing to see if
local high school students or community members may be interested in applying.
e. Other Items:
i. FRREA Contract: We are still waiting for the FRREA final contract with the edits
based on negotiation agreements. We are proceeding with the agreed terms until
we have a document to sign.
ii. Building Works: PA work is complete; floors and deep cleaning are currently
underway.
iii. District Treasurer Transition: Sharon Harrison has been confirmed to be taking
over as the District Treasurer (formerly Jane Gleason).
5. New Business: Resignation of School Committee Member
a. Douglas Miner, a School Committee Member from Sandisfield, has resigned, opting to
focus his time on the Sandisfield Fire Department.
b. The town of Sandisfield is working to seek a replacement. The town must fill the seat
within 3 school committee meetings. If they cannot fill the seat in time, they will
temporarily fill it with a Select Board member until it is filled. Interested parties should
send their interest to Jane at the Sandisfield Town Office.
6. Old Business: Options for District Leadership Structure 2027-2028
a. Superintendent Lee gave a recap of the last school committee meeting where they
discussed strategic priorities and administration leadership structure options. This topic
is up for discussion due to Superintendent Lee’s decision to retire following the
2026-2027 school year, which causes some urgency. Leadership structure they have
discussed so far include:
i. Full Time (FT) Principal/Part Time (PT) Superintendent
ii. FT Principal/Superintendent Combo
iii. FT Principal Shared Superintendent
iv. FT Principal Contract District Admin with consultant agency
v. The discussed but are not interested currently in:
1. FT Principal, join another school district
2. FT Principal Superintendent Union (relationship with neighboring towns)
b. Following the discussion at the last meeting, strongest options were FT Principal/PT
Superintendent/FT Director, or FT Principal/Superintendent (closest district that mirrors
this is Richmond, w/ PT Director of Student Services)
i. Superintendent Lee spoke with Beth, Richmond’s Principal/Superintendent (who
became Superintendent through this process), who had nothing but good things
to say about the combined role. He described the process for becoming a
certified Superintendent.
c. The School Committee discussed next steps for seeking district leadership options,
noting a few different organizations that assist with superintendent searches.
d. The committee discussed which combinations of the 3 roles
(Principal/Superintendent/Director of Student Services) are possible. The Director of
Student Services can be the Superintendent (local example = Hancock); however, the
Director of Student Services and Principal roles conflict because the IEP process
requires these roles to be separate.
FRRSD School Committee Meeting #483 - 8.10.2026 2 of 3
e. There was a question about how some of these combined roles would be implemented
(such as moving forward with a combined Principal/Superintendent role if Laurie Flower
is still Principal). Superintendent Lee provided suggestions on how to proceed,
depending on what we are looking for and the timeline to fill it/retirement plans for the
other district leadership positions.
f. The Committee discussed when to proceed with the search process relative to
understanding the candidate landscape, and discussed contacting MASC for guidance.
i. At the next school committee meeting, looking for a unanimous decision on a
combined vs. separate Principal/Superintendent. The School Committee would
like input from staff and community members.
1. They discussed a survey with a forum follow-up, one-to-one or group
discussions, and analysis of the results, including the leadership facets
most needed to define the position description, along with the survey and
forum structure. Consider using hiring consultants to help facilitate the
survey/discussion to help neutralize the discussion.
ii. There was a discussion on the timeline: do a survey soon with results by
November, when we have a decision from Laurie on her long-term plan, and then
proceed with hiring in December. There were concerns that December is too late
in the process, and what our options are if we don’t find someone by July 2027.
1. Superintendent Lee noted that, as a last resort, he can continue on a per
diem rate if the role/combined role has not been filled by July 2027.
2. There was dicussion on framing this as a longer-term planning process to
keep options open.
g. Next Steps:
i. Contact MASC
ii. Follow up with Stacey Schultze to fill her in on the conversation so they are
prepared to narrow down district leadership options
iii. Contact superintendent search consultant agencies
iv. Review Data on Administration FTE in comparison to our district.
v. Begin working on survey questions
vi. There is discussion on hearing from Laurie directly on her perspective, both as
an administrator and as a staff member who has worked here under both
structures, and Mike. Tim will speak with both of them before the next meeting.
7. Warrants for Review:
a. Warrants are available in the front office if anyone would like to review them.
8. Other Items not anticipated
a. Nothing at this time
9. Adjournment:
a. Carl Nett made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 7:06 PM.
i. Kate Meierdicks seconded the motion.
ii. VOTE - Roll Call: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett
Respectfully submitted,
Caroline Stamm

Farmington River Regional School District
School Committee
Meeting #484 Farmington River Elementary School Library
Monday, September 14th, 2026
MINUTES
6:00 PM
Members Present: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett, Stacey Schultze
Also Present: Superintendent Timothy Lee, Caroline Stamm
1. Call to Order: The meeting was called to order at 6:00 PM by Denise Hardie.
a. Roll Call: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett Stacey Schultze.
2. Special Agenda Item: Recognition of Ms. Jane Gleason
a. Denise introduced Ms. Jane Gleason, who has served as the District Treasuerer for the
duration of the Regional School District for the past 34 years. Denise acknowledged all
of Jane’s wonderful contributions, guidance, and stability in her tenure, and wishes her
well with her future plans with her family and her time.
b. Many members of the district community shared their appreciation for her and warm
wishes, including Denise Hardie, Carl Nett, Carol Sauerhoefer, Laurie Flower, Heidi
Utenis, among others.
3. Public Comment:
a. Denise handed out a Back to School Ballot about the top 5 things we like about
Farmington River. There was a question about what Dragon Cards/Eggs are, which
Laurie Flower was able to explain.
4. Review of Minutes:
- Regular Meeting of August 10th, 2026
a. MOTION: Carl Nett made a motion to approve minutes from Meeting #483 (8/10/26).
i. Kate Meierdicks seconded the motion.
ii. There was no discussion.
iii. VOTE to accept: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, and Carl Nett were in favor.
Stacey Schultze abstained from the vote. There were no objections, and the
motion passed to approve minutes from Meeting #483 (8/10/26).
b. The minutes from the July Meeting were postponed to the next meeting.
5. Superintendent’s Report:
a. Opening of School Report (LF)
i. Principal Laurie Flower began by thanking Stacey Schultze, who appeared as a
representative from the School Committee on the first day PD, and for leading the
staff on the “Give, Get, Grateful” exercise
ii. Laurie spoke about the strong start to the school year, and how staff has put a
great deal of work into establishing routines and expectations with students.
iii. The school held a Welcome Assembly last Friday and discussed what makes a
great school. Students had great input on how to improve our school community!
FRRSD School Committee Meeting #484 - 9.14.2026 1 of 5
iv. We are welcoming 16 new students - 8 of whom are school choice, with 2 more
expected to begin in October.
v. We are continuing to build on the implementations from last year (new reading
curriculum, assessment system, SIS, etc) and added new phones and PA system
as we continue to focus on improving and training safety systems and protocols.
vi. We are still working on the PRISM grant, and received praise from the state on
the successes of that implementation goals - noting outstanding work with critical
thinking, student self-expression, etc.
vii. We received recognition from the state for our attendance as well.
b. Transportation Update (MS)
i. Mike Sporito, who oversees transportation as part of his role as Director of
Student Services, shared updates on our transportation this year - noting that we
are operating a 5-van fleet following last year’s purchase. He recognized Heidi
Utenis’ contributions to aid with coverage - specifically her contributions to cover
the morning high school & elementary runs.
ii. We are working with Dufour for their 3-bus fleet.
1. There have been some issues that are still being ironed out. He noted that
we are closing the gap daily towards improving routes to get closer to the
times that parents were originally scheduled.
iii. Superintendent Lee recognized the hard work of Mike Saporito for coordinating
the transportation, as well driving a van himself.
c. 2026-2027 Enrollment as of 9/14
i. With the additions of the new family coming in October that Laurie mentioned, we
are nearing the same number of students that we ended last year with.
ii. K-6th grade class sizes are between 11 and 16, with the smallest classes in K, 2,
3 and largest 4th and 6th.
iii. PK/EK has somewhere between 17-18 in the AM and 10 in the PM with 2
teachers in the room.
d. Afterschool Program Update
i. Superintendent Lee shared the unfortunate news that the LYA was not able to
provide the after-school program as planned due to staffing shortages.
ii. The Admin Team decided to bring back the After-School “Dragons Den” program
that has been run in the past few years. He shared the flyer about the program
and anticipates that this will be shared with families soon. The program would
begin on Sept. 29th.
6. New Business:
a. MOU Afterschool (Dragon’s Den) Program Hourly Stipends
i. Superintendent Lee noted that in his review of the FRREA contract, he noticed
that there was no language for the general Afterschool Program outside of
activity-based programs (such as Intramurals, Chess Club, Snowshoeing, etc). In
the past, they have run the program without a school-committee-approved MOU.
ii. He brought forth a proposed MOU for the 2026-2027 Stipend for Afterschool
Program (Dragon’s Den) Staff. He noted that this applies to Unit A & C members
since the position applies to members from both units.
FRRSD School Committee Meeting #484 - 9.14.2026 2 of 5
iii. There was discussion on comparing the Dragon Den’s program to the proposed
LYA afterschool program - noting the LYA was more comprehensive, but required
the families to pay, but and due to the certification of LYA, parents could use
vouchers. Part of this comparison was viewing after school program as more of
an enrichment program compared to regular childcare option for working parents.
iv. There was a discussion that the MOU presented has up to 3 positions, which
gives the admin team flexibility for increasing enrollment.
v. There was clarification regarding that the MOU requires that the positions hired
must be part of the FRREA Bargaining Unit since this is an MOU for the union
contract.
vi. MOTION: Carl Nett made a motion to approve the Afterschool Care MOU as
presented.
1. Stacey Schultze seconded the motion.
2. There was no discussion.
3. VOTE to accept: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett, and Stacey
Schultze were in favor. There were no objections, and the motion passed
unanimously 4-0 to approve the Afterschool Staff MOU as presented.
b. Staff Opening Day Activity: Responses
i. Superintendent Lee thanked Stacey for coming to the PD day and welcoming the
staff back on behalf of the school committee, and for leading the staff through the
“Give, Get, Grateful” activity.
ii. Stacey explained the activity was and the background on what this activity was
seeking. She asked staff 1 thing they can give to FRES, 1 thing they’d like to get,
and 1 thing that they are grateful for.
1. She noted that there was overwhelming need for support but was not
exactly clear on what that support looks like, so they would need to dive in
further on what that means.
2. She also noted that everyone was grateful for the community that was
built.
3. There was discussion on perhaps repeating the activity with the parents
to see their perspective.
iii. Superintendent Lee responded that his ‘ah-ha” moment is seeing that staff wants
to feel appreciated for their work, and noted on how he and the admin team can
better share this appreciation with staff directly.
c. Monthly Agenda Placeholder for Staff News & Program Highlights
i. They discussed that adding this agenda item placeholder as a response to the
“Give, Get, Grateful” activity.
ii. MOTION: Carl Nett made a motion to add an agenda item placeholder for Staff
News & Program Highlights on future agendas moving forward.
1. Stacey Schultze seconded the motion.
2. The discussion was to aim to add this beginning in October.
3. VOTE to accept: Denise Hardie, Kate Meierdiercks, Carl Nett, and Stacey
